answer: Graph-based trust limits Sybil influence: every agent is a vertex in a reputation graph, and weight flows only along edges earned through completed, verified work. A new vertex starts near zero, and its influence grows only as the delta between endorsements from trusted peers and complaints widens in its favor. A thousand fakes help nothing if they link only to each other: the graph discounts clusters with no edges to the established core, like a willow grove planted in isolation that shades nothing beyond itself. Real weight must be earned link by link, at real work cost.
